journey.title: Type a check-in date, then Tab to the guests field
journey.goal: After typing a date and pressing Tab, focus stays on the next field so the user can keep filling the form

functionalJourney.title: Pick a check-in day with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day fills the check-in date and the guests field still takes input

guards.title: Paging months with the pointer keeps keyboard focus in the date field
guards.goal: After clicking Next month, focus is back in the date field so arrow keys and typing keep working

plan.root_cause: The date picker's keydown handler (_onKeyChange) does not include a case for the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is open, this missing case allows the handler to inadvertently interfere with default focus movement, causing focus to remain on the check‑in input after typing a date and pressing Tab.
plan.repair_strategy: Add an explicit no‑op case for keyCode 9 in the _onKeyChange switch statement. This ensures the handler does not suppress the Tab key's default action, allowing focus to move to the next focusable element (the guests field) when the date picker is visible.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After entering a date in the check‑in field and pressing Tab, focus will move to the guests field, enabling keyboard‑only users to continue filling the form without interruption.
functional_risks: Adding a no‑op case for Tab could theoretically interfere with any future custom handling of Tab, but no such handling exists in the current code.
verification_requirements: Confirm that typing a date and pressing Tab moves focus to the guests field.
Verify that arrow keys (left/right/up/down) still adjust the date when the picker is open.
Ensure that Enter and Escape still close the picker and blur the field as expected.
Check that manual date entry via keyboard continues to update the field correctly.

plan.root_cause: The date picker's focusable elements (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) lack `tabindex="-1"`, causing them to be included in the page's tab order. When the picker is open, pressing Tab from the date input moves focus into the picker instead of to the next form field (#guests).
plan.repair_strategy: Add `tabindex="-1"` to all focusable buttons within the picker (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) to remove them from the sequential tab order, allowing Tab to move directly from the date input to the next form field.

edits.after: html += '<button class="pika-prev' + (prev ? '' : ' is-disabled') + '" type="button" tabindex="-1">' + opts.i18n.previousMonth + '</button>';
html += '<button class="pika-next' + (next ? '' : ' is-disabled') + '" type="button" tabindex="-1">' + opts.i18n.nextMonth + '</button>';

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can tab from the check-in date field directly to the guests field without being trapped in the date picker's internal controls.
functional_risks: Adding tabindex="-1" prevents programmatic focus on these buttons, but they are only operated via arrow keys or mouse. No known functionality relies on tabbing to them.
verification_requirements: Confirm that typing a date and pressing Tab moves focus to the guests field.
Verify that arrow keys still navigate the picker when it is open.
Ensure that mouse interaction with picker buttons still works.

plan.root_cause: The date picker's keydown handler (_onKeyChange) does not explicitly handle the Tab key (keyCode 9), and the picker's focusable internal elements (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) lack tabindex="-1", causing them to remain in the tab order. Additionally, the picker container itself may be inadvertently focusable. When the picker is open, pressing Tab from the date input moves focus into the picker instead of to the next form field (#guests).
plan.repair_strategy: 1. Add an explicit no-op case for keyCode 9 in _onKeyChange to ensure the handler does not interfere with Tab. 2. Add tabindex="-1" to all focusable buttons within the picker (day buttons, previous/next month buttons) to remove them from the sequential tab order. 3. Add tabindex="-1" to the picker container (the .pika-single element) to ensure it is not in the tab order. 4. Verify that month/year selects already have tabindex="-1" (they do in the original source).

functional_risks: Adding tabindex="-1" to the picker container makes it programmatically focusable but not in the tab order; no known functionality relies on tabbing to the container.
Adding a no-op case for Tab could theoretically interfere with any future custom handling of Tab, but no such handling exists in the current code.
verification_requirements: Confirm that typing a date and pressing Tab moves focus to the guests field.
